approved_scope.title: Refuse review status and finalize of a change already archived on the remote default and name it
approved_scope.description: Refuse review status and finalize of a change already archived on the remote default and name it
acceptance_criteria: Both cases are integration tests built from the auditor's squash steps. Every other gate, including finalize's trusted-transition preflight, is unchanged.

For that change, `change status` and `change ship-status` report it as already archived upstream with the same reference, commit and next step. The handoff is never `safe` and the next action is never `finalize` or `ship`.

When the remote default branch (or HEAD history) already holds an archive of the same change id, `change review` refuses before recording acceptance. The refusal names the change, the reference and the commit that archived it, and gives the next step: merge or rebase onto the remote default, whose archive is authoritative. The change is not moved to `accepted`.
Without an upstream archive, a change verified on a branch and squash-merged onto its base before finalize still passes `change review` and `change finalize` archives it (regression guard for #690).
`change finalize` on that change refuses with the same named cause instead of "requires exactly one trusted transition ... found 0". It still refuses: no second archive is written.

approved_scope.description: Refuse review status and finalize of a change already archived on the remote default and name it
acceptance_criteria: An archive that `HEAD` already contains is not refused: that is the reopen-and-rearchive path, which keeps working unchanged.
Both cases are integration tests built from the auditor's squash steps. Every other gate, including finalize's trusted-transition preflight, is unchanged.

For a refused change, `change status` and `change ship-status` report it as already archived upstream with the same reference, commit and next step. The handoff is never `safe` and the next action is never `finalize` or `ship`.

When the remote default branch holds an archive of the same change id and `HEAD` does not contain that archive, `change review` refuses before recording acceptance. The refusal names the change, the reference and the commit that archived it, and gives the next step: merge or rebase onto the remote default, whose archive is authoritative. The change is not moved to `accepted`.
Without an upstream archive, a change verified on a branch and squash-merged onto its base before finalize still passes `change review` and `change finalize` archives it (regression guard for #690).
`change finalize` on that change refuses with the same named cause instead of "requires exactly one trusted transition ... found 0". It still refuses: no second archive is written.

The criteria and REQ-change-127 said 'archived in reachable history (HEAD or the remote default)'; the implementation refuses only an archive the remote default has and HEAD does not, because an archive already in HEAD is the reopen-and-rearchive path. applied_items.content:
The system SHALL refuse `change review` and `change finalize`, and SHALL NOT report readiness `safe` from `change status` or `change ship-status`, for a change whose id is already archived in reachable history (HEAD or the remote default) while its own record is not archived. The refusal SHALL name the reference and commit of that archive and the next step: merge or rebase onto that reference.

Acceptance Criteria
- With the remote default holding an archive of the change, `change review` refuses before recording acceptance and the record stays `verifying`.
- `change finalize` refuses with the same named cause and writes no archive.
- Without an upstream archive, a squash before finalize still reviews and finalizes.

`change status` and `change ship-status` SHALL report a change that is already archived upstream with the reference, the archive commit and the next step, in text and JSON, and SHALL NOT name finalize or ship as its next action.

Acceptance Criteria
- Text output names the reference, commit and the merge or rebase step.
- JSON readiness is not `safe`.
